blocks.content: J&K's temperate-Himalayan ecology supports a distinctive set of protected areas and flagship species, several found nowhere else in India — this chapter is a favourite source of species-and-park-name pairing questions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India's Protected Area Network is constituted under the Wildlife Protection Act (WPA), 1972, encompassing National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and Conservation Reserves.
Project Tiger was launched in 1973 to safeguard the flagship Bengal Tiger species, starting from Jim Corbett National Park.
Biosphere Reserves conserve entire ecosystems with designated Core, Buffer, and Transition zones under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme.
Flagship species like the Great One-Horned Rhinoceros, Asiatic Lion, and Snow Leopard are conserved through targeted regional protection initiatives.
Key environmental threats include habitat fragmentation, human-wildlife conflict, climate change, and illegal wildlife trade.

blocks.content: India's protected area network forms the backbone of biodiversity conservation across diverse ecosystems.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Dachigam National Park's association with the Hangul (Kashmir stag) is one of the single most frequently tested species-and-park pairings for J&K — the Hangul is critically endangered and Dachigam is essentially its last significant wild stronghold.

items: Hangul (Kashmir stag, Cervus hanglu hanglu) — J&K's state animal; critically endangered, with its last significant wild population concentrated in and around Dachigam National Park; considered one of India's most endangered mammal species.

Snow leopard — found in the higher-altitude reaches of J&K's mountain ranges (and more extensively in neighbouring Ladakh); an elusive, globally vulnerable big cat that has become a flagship species for high-altitude conservation efforts across the wider Himalayan region.

Himalayan black bear and Himalayan brown bear — both found in J&K's forested and higher-altitude zones respectively, with periodic human-wildlife conflict incidents (particularly involving black bears near populated forest-fringe areas) a recurring local news and wildlife-management topic.
Markhor (a large wild goat species with distinctive spiral horns) — found in parts of the Pir Panjal range, another species of significant conservation concern in the wider region.
Distinction between National Parks (no human rights allowed) and Wildlife Sanctuaries (limited rights permitted) is frequently tested in Prelims.
Memorize key environmental legislation years: WPA (1972), Water Act (1974), Forest Conservation Act (1980), and Environment Protection Act (1986).
Pay attention to the 12 Indian Biosphere Reserves designated under UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR).

Dal Lake's shrinking area and declining water quality (due to encroachment, sewage inflow, and silt accumulation) has been a long-running environmental concern and the subject of sustained conservation/dredging efforts by the Lakes and Waterways Development Authority (LAWDA) and successor bodies.

Glacial retreat across the Kashmir Valley's glacier systems (Chapter 3), including the Kolahoi Glacier, has been documented by glaciological studies and is linked to wider Himalayan climate-change trends, with implications for long-term river-flow reliability.

Deforestation pressure, particularly historically from the timber trade and more recently from infrastructure development and tourism-linked construction, remains an ongoing forest-management concern across the Valley's temperate coniferous forest zones (Chapter 4).
Hangul (Kashmir stag) = J&K's state animal; critically endangered; last significant wild population in Dachigam National Park.
Dachigam National Park (near Srinagar) is the flagship protected area of J&K proper; Hemis National Park (major snow leopard habitat) lies in the separate Ladakh UT.
Kishtwar National Park protects Himalayan musk deer and snow leopard habitat.
Dal Lake's environmental decline (encroachment, sewage, silt) is a long-running conservation concern, addressed by LAWDA and successor bodies.
